Definition: from G1909 and G2288; doomed to death:--appointed to death.
BiblicalUsage: Epithanatios means appointed to death, doomed to die — and Paul says, I think God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death, for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.
TheologicalSignificance: Last, exposed, appointed to death — and yet the gospel advanced on men the world counted as dying, and that is Paul's spectacle.
